# Tests that skip at CELERIS_MAX_IOURING_TIER=base on purpose, for .github/scripts/base-tier-tally.sh
# (celeris#890 item 87): the full test or subtest name, then why. A name covers its own
# subtests. Measured on the run of the job iouring-base-tier cited in the pull request:
# 554 top-level tests passed, 4 skipped at the top level, 12 SKIP lines in all. On main
# 8936e89 (with #1123 and #1127) a docker run (kernel without an fe80:: address) gave 577
# passed and 13 SKIP lines, the 13th being TestListenOnAZonedLinkLocalServes885, which
# the job does not allow: it sets CELERIS_REQUIRE_ZONED_PEER=1, so the test fails rather
# than skips on a runner without one.
min-pass 540

# Tier base has no multishot recv with provided buffers (the tests say so in their skip).
TestSpentDetectBudgetReturnsItsRingBuffer/check no provided buffer ring at the base tier
TestSpentDetectBudgetReturnsItsRingBuffer/recheck no provided buffer ring at the base tier
TestSpentDetectBudgetReturnsItsRingBuffer/check-async no provided buffer ring at the base tier
TestSpentDetectBudgetReturnsItsRingBuffer/recheck-async no provided buffer ring at the base tier
TestStartupLineReportsTheMultishotRecvThatIsInUse/unset tier base has no multishot recv
TestStartupLineReportsTheMultishotRecvThatIsInUse/zero tier base has no multishot recv
TestStartupLineReportsTheMultishotRecvThatIsInUse/true-is-not-1 tier base has no multishot recv
TestStartupLineReportsTheMultishotRecvThatIsInUse/one tier base has no multishot recv
TestMultishotRecvDecidedOnceAtNew/on_at_New,_off_after tier base has no multishot recv
TestMultishotRecvDecidedOnceAtNew/off_at_New,_on_after tier base has no multishot recv

# They need net.ipv4.tcp_synack_retries=0; the runner has 5. The step "celeris#662
# tcp_synack_retries=0 guard" of the job adaptive sets it and forbids the skip.
TestPauseAcceptServesDeferredIdleConnectionsSynackRetriesZero needs net.ipv4.tcp_synack_retries=0
TestPauseAcceptNoGuardLosesAtSynackRetriesZero needs net.ipv4.tcp_synack_retries=0

# They skip by design on a host that cannot make the condition they test (the test's own skip
# message says which). No step forces them to run; on other hosts they run and pass. A skip of
# either is allowed only with its own reason in the log: base-tier-tally.sh allows the name, and
# .github/scripts/host-skip-reason.sh (called by the job right after it) checks the reason, so the
# same tests' other skips (no io_uring, a failed setrlimit, no loopback) still fail the job.
#   * TestStartFDLEngineRidesOutRingENOMEM fills the 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK budget with rings and
#     skips ("could not fill the memlock budget (512 rings held)") when 512 rings fit at that soft
#     limit. All five jobs observed on the runner kernel 7.0.0-1020-azure (runs 44727244397,
#     44732627322, 44836576779 base tier; 44836534678, 44836576779 unit job) skipped it for this
#     reason; the jobs observed on 7.0.0-1019-azure and 7.0.0-1016-aws ran and passed it. Why that
#     kernel lets the rings in is not established.
#   * TestDialWatchDescribesTheSocketsOfAPort1229 skips when the host does not leave a dial to the
#     reserved 10.255.255.1 unanswered (run 43528508636, 7.0.0-1014-aws).
TestStartFDLEngineRidesOutRingENOMEM 512 rings fit at the 8 MiB memlock soft limit on this host, so the budget cannot be filled
TestDialWatchDescribesTheSocketsOfAPort1229 this host does not leave a dial to 10.255.255.1 unanswered
